The search turned up a clear way to turn off automatic stream resumption on the client, but the sources conflict on whether chat recovery can be turned off on the server.

**Disabling stream resumption (client side):** The resumable-streaming docs for `agents` 0.24.0 show a `resume: false` option passed to `useAgentChat`. That option turns off automatic resumption, which is useful for short responses. ([unpkg agents 0.24.0 docs](https://unpkg.com/agents@0.24.0/docs/resumable-streaming.md))

**Chat recovery (server side), by version:**
- **`@cloudflare/ai-chat` 0.9.x package page:** AIChatAgent defaults chatRecovery to false. Enable it when you want chat turns to survive Worker deploys, Durable Object eviction, or process restarts. In this version, leaving it unset is the way to keep it off. ([Socket, v0.9.0](https://socket.dev/npm/package/@cloudflare/ai-chat/overview/0.9.0))
- **`agents` 0.20.1 docs:** Recovery is opt-in. Plain `AIChatAgent` subclasses use `override chatRecovery = true` to turn it on. ([unpkg agents 0.20.1 docs](https://unpkg.com/agents@0.20.1/docs/resumable-streaming.md) / [app.unpkg mirror](https://app.unpkg.com/agents@0.20.1/files/docs/resumable-streaming.md))
- **`agents` 0.24.0 docs:** This conflicts with the older guidance. Durable Object eviction recovery is also always enabled for AIChatAgent and Think: every turn runs inside a recoverable fiber. Use chatRecovery only to tune its budgets and terminal behavior. ([app.unpkg mirror, 0.24.0](https://app.unpkg.com/agents@0.24.0/files/docs/resumable-streaming.md))

**Bottom line:** If you're on a version like 0.24.0, the docs suggest server-side eviction recovery can't be disabled, and `chatRecovery` only adjusts its limits. Check the exact version you have installed. If you're on 0.9.x, leaving `chatRecovery` unset keeps it off. The `resume: false` client option is the documented way to stop resumption on reconnect. I didn't find an explicit server-side switch to fully disable recovery in the 0.24.0 docs, so check the current Cloudflare Agents documentation or the GitHub repo if you need certainty.

The page doesn't document `chatRecovery` beyond one sentence. It doesn't specify what `false` does, the accepted values, the budgets, or the terminal behavior.

**`chatRecovery`**
- "Use `chatRecovery` only to tune its budgets and terminal behavior."

**Always-on recovery**
- "This is client reconnect recovery, not Durable Object eviction recovery."
- "Durable Object eviction recovery is also always enabled for `AIChatAgent` and `Think`"
- "every turn runs inside a recoverable fiber."

**Disabling client resume**
- "If you do not want automatic resume (for example, for short responses), disable it:"
- Set `resume: false` in `useAgentChat`.

**Discarding or abandoning an interrupted turn**
The page doesn't describe a discard API. It covers these related behaviors:
- Client cleanup is local by default: "Generic client stream abort/cleanup is local-only by default." Setting `cancelOnClientAbort: true` makes client lifecycle cancel the server turn.
- An explicit stop cancels the server turn: "An explicit `stop()` still cancels the server turn."
- Buffers are reclaimed automatically: "A buffer a crash left behind is reclaimed when the next stream starts," with "abandoned in-flight streams after 1 hour without a chunk."
- Stale streams are cleaned up: "Stale streams (older than 5 minutes) are cleaned up on restore."

input.prompt: Quote verbatim all text about chatRecovery: its type, accepted values (boolean? object?), what false means, budgets, terminal behavior, onChatRecovery hook and its return options (e.g. continue/persist/skip).

toolu_019jTuVwCh7q16fzBfC3kuJG.prompt: Quote verbatim all text about chatRecovery: its type, accepted values (boolean? object?), what false means, budgets, terminal behavior, onChatRecovery hook and its return options (e.g. continue/persist/skip).

content.content:
The page doesn't say what types `chatRecovery` accepts or what `false` does. It shows only an object-literal example, and the hook's return options are documented separately.

**Overview and placement**

- "Durable recovery is always enabled. Use `chatRecovery` only to tune its budgets and terminal behavior."
- "Assign `chatRecovery` as a class field or in the constructor — never in `onStart()`."
- The example uses `override chatRecovery = { ... }` as a class field.

**Budget and terminal fields** (defaults from the configuration table)

- `maxAttempts` (default `10`): "Attempt cap before terminal exhaustion."
- `stableTimeoutMs` (default `10_000`): "How long a recovery attempt waits for the isolate to reach stable state before rescheduling."
- `terminalMessage` (default: generic message): "The message shown to the user when recovery is given up on."
- `noProgressTimeoutMs` (default `300_000`, 5 min): "how long an incident may go without forward progress before it is sealed"
- `maxRecoveryWork` (default `1000`): "Maximum produced content/tool units since the incident began," and it is a "Runaway-loop guard."
- `maxOomRetries` (default `3`): "Tight retry budget for the specific case of a Durable Object isolate exceeding its memory limit and being reset mid-turn." "Set `0` to seal on the first OOM."
- `shouldKeepRecovering`: "Caller policy consulted from the second recovery attempt onward."
- `onExhausted`: "Called once when recovery is given up on, before the terminal message is delivered."

**Terminal sealing reasons (`ctx.reason`)**

Recovery is sealed only by these values: `no_progress_timeout`, `max_attempts_exceeded`, `work_budget_exceeded`, `out_of_memory`, `recovery_aborted` (your `shouldKeepRecovering` returned `false`), and `stable_timeout`.

**`onChatRecovery` hook**

- Signature: `override async onChatRecovery(ctx: ChatRecoveryContext): Promise<ChatRecoveryOptions>`
- Default: "The default behavior persists the partial response and schedules a continuation via `continueLastTurn()`."
- Return options (`ChatRecoveryOptions`):
  - `persist` (default `true`): "Save the partial response as an assistant message"
  - `continue` (default `true`): "Schedule a continuation via `continueLastTurn()`"
- Common return values:
  - `{}`: "persist partial + auto-continue (default, works with providers that support assistant prefill)"
  - `{ continue: false }`: "persist partial but do not auto-continue (handle continuation yourself)"
  - `{ persist: false, continue: false }`: "do not persist the unsettled remainder and handle everything yourself"
- "Settled work is never dropped: `persist: false` only suppresses persistence of a partial that has nothing settled to lose."

The page documents no `skip` option. The closest equivalent is `persist: false`, combined with `continue: false`.

content.text:
Probably not, on current versions. It depends on which version you're running.

**On recent `agents` versions (e.g. 0.24.0), `chatRecovery: false` won't turn recovery off.** The docs say "Durable recovery is always enabled. Use `chatRecovery` only to tune its budgets and terminal behavior." Every turn runs inside a recoverable fiber. `chatRecovery` is documented only as an object of settings (`maxAttempts`, `maxOomRetries`, `noProgressTimeoutMs`, `onExhausted`, etc.). Setting it to `false` isn't documented to do anything.

**On older versions (`@cloudflare/ai-chat` 0.9.x / `agents` ~0.20), recovery was opt-in and off by default.** You only turned it on with `override chatRecovery = true`. There, leaving it unset already gives you what you want.

### What to do on current versions

**1. Stop the server from auto-continuing interrupted turns.** Override `onChatRecovery`:

```ts
export class MyAgent extends AIChatAgent<Env> {
  override async onChatRecovery(ctx) {
    // Don't save the unfinished partial, don't call continueLastTurn()
    return { persist: false, continue: false };
  }
}
```

- `{ continue: false }` keeps the partial response but doesn't resume.
- `{ persist: false, continue: false }` also drops the unsaved partial. Work that was already settled (e.g. completed tool results) is always kept.

**2. Stop the client from reattaching to an in-progress stream on reconnect.** This is a separate mechanism:

```ts
const chat = useAgentChat({ agent, resume: false });
```

**3. Optionally, make a client disconnect or abort cancel the server turn.** Use `cancelOnClientAbort: true`; by default a client abort only cleans up locally. An explicit `stop()` always cancels the server turn.

If you want recovery to give up almost immediately rather than just not continuing, you can also set small budgets, e.g. `override chatRecovery = { maxAttempts: 1, maxOomRetries: 0 }`. Step 1 is the cleaner fix. Check your installed `agents` / `@cloudflare/ai-chat` version first to see which behavior applies.

Sources:
- [agents 0.24.0 – resumable-streaming.md](https://unpkg.com/agents@0.24.0/docs/resumable-streaming.md) ([mirror](https://app.unpkg.com/agents@0.24.0/files/docs/resumable-streaming.md))
- [agents 0.24.0 – chat-agents.md](https://unpkg.com/agents@0.24.0/docs/chat-agents.md)
- [agents 0.20.1 – resumable-streaming.md](https://unpkg.com/agents@0.20.1/docs/resumable-streaming.md) ([mirror](https://app.unpkg.com/agents@0.20.1/files/docs/resumable-streaming.md))
- [@cloudflare/ai-chat 0.9.0 (Socket)](https://socket.dev/npm/package/@cloudflare/ai-chat/overview/0.9.0)
